items.title: ShackStream: Elden Ring on The Stevetendo Show! Episode 757
items.summary: Time to take down some bosses in Elden Ring.
items.content:
Video ShackStream: Elden Ring on The Stevetendo Show! Episode 757 Time to take down some bosses in Elden Ring.

Tonight, on The Stevetendo Show, we're diving right back into our Elden Ring playthrough. This game is as tough as I thought it was going to be. On the plus side, we have actually made some progress. It took a long time, but we took down the Tree Sentinel at the start of the game . I can only imagine what some of the other bosses will look like if the Tree Sentinel was kicking my face in, but I digress.

Case in point, we're up to Margit, the first major boss in the game, and I'm having a tough time. We might have to grind for levels to get stronger. That was the plan before we took on the Tree Sentinel and stayed there for about an hour. Elden Ring and games like it are all about trial and error, learning the attack patterns. Will I be able to defeat Margit and progress? Set to go live at 5 p.m. PT/8 p.m. ET, join The Stevetendo Show for more of our Elden Ring playthrough.

Shackers who want to join in on the fun can head over to the Shacknews Twitch channel, where you can tune into The Stevetendo Show every Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday.

Be sure to check out the Shacknews Twitch channel and the Shacknews VODs YouTube channel. Catch up on some of your favorite Shacknews programs with a subscription to the YouTube channel and a follow to the Twitch channel. If you aren’t aware, Shacknews has a new service for you called Shackmaps . The lovely Shacknews staff has gone through some of your favorite video games to keep you from getting lost. There are new maps coming soon, so sign up now!

It's October so start coming up with some scary games that you want to see me play on The Stevetendo Show. All I ask is that the game is either on the Nintendo Switch eShop or one of the Nintendo Switch Online services. We have fun playing spooky games on the show because I usually don't know anything about them. Be on the lookout for the new Castlevania game starting up soon on The Stevetendo Show since I loved the demo.

items.title: Opinion: Elden Ring Is One Of My Favourite Games That I've Hardly Played
items.content:
I have started a new Elden Ring save file on four separate occasions now, and I have absolutely adored my time with each of them. And yet, despite putting 15-20 hours minimum into each new load, my current Switch 2 playthrough is the first time that I've managed to push through the 'tutorial area'.

I need to do some explaining here, because if you have never ventured into the Lands Between, then three save files and 60+ hours spent in a tutorial sounds insane. However, in the grand scheme of things, it's not that bad .

After pushing you through a very brief 'real' tutorial — one that introduces you to the basics of Elden Ring's combat and movement — your Tarnished avatar is funnelled into Limgrave and beckoned towards Stormveil Castle as your first major objective. However, rushing straight to the battlements will put you up against foes and challenges that you are severely underprepared for, so the game encourages you to instead take a stroll around the area and perhaps venture down to the locales south of it in the Weeping Peninsula.

Much like Breath of the Wild 's Great Plateau, this is the game's actual tutorial. But I cannot stress this enough, it makes Link's wakeup spot look tiny.

Limgrave and its surrounding areas are huge and so densely packed with things to do that one could happily play this zone as a game of its own. Heck, for my first three save files, that's exactly what I did.

I explored the nooks and crannies of all the region's catacombs, took on mini bosses and Minor Erdtrees, solved environmental puzzles to unlock new gear, and took on sidequests that involved storylines and platforming challenges of their own.

On my first save back in 2022, by the time that I finally pushed through the game's first 'roadblock' boss, Margit (yes, there is a way around him, but I didn't see that at the time), I was quite content with the 20-odd hours I had put into Elden Ring, and I went off to play something else. Save files two and three saw me go further still, through the game's first real dungeon and into the boss on the other side. On both these occasions, I polished off Godrick the Grafted (a proper FromSoft name, if I've ever heard one) with relative ease, but was deterred by what awaited me afterwards: the proper game .

Just like the first time that you paraglide off the Great Plateau and realise everything you've explored up to this point is just a tiny proportion of what the whole map has to offer, stepping into Lunaria of the Lakes is a similarly daunting task. The zone's entry point even has a vantage point vaguely reminiscent of leaving the Shrine of Resurrection, for crying out loud.

For save files two and three, the scope of what was to come was simply too much. I had had a wonderful time with everything I had played up until that point, and loved how it all culminated in a challenging dungeon and gruesome boss. Honestly, I couldn't bring myself to do it all over again.

Until the Tarnished Edition arrived on Switch 2, that is. I finally got around to starting save file number four a few weeks back, and believe me when I say, I have not been able to put it down.

I did my usual Limgrave exploration, ventured into the fiery Caelid region (and swiftly realised I was still far too weak for it), and steadily levelled up in various catacombs and hoard encounters. Unsurprisingly, I dispatched both Margit and Godrick in one or two attempts — I've played 'em both more than enough by now — and Stormveil was similarly breezy for someone who's spent so much time in it over the years. But then something unexpected happened: I kept playing.

Despite my previous cowardice, I stepped boldly into the uncharted waters of 'The Lakes' and I still haven't quit. As I am writing this, I have just polished off The Academy of Raya Lucaria (a dungeon that, as someone using a magic build, can get in the bin) and its Good Boi / Bad Gurl bosses, and I still want more.

Aside from the portability perk — I couldn't put this version down, even if I wanted to — the Switch 2 port itself is absolutely sublime. All those months of convention footage and delays had me worried that I'd never be able to play a game this reliant on reaction times with a choppy frame rate, but it all holds up remarkably well. Performance certainly hasn't been perfect, and I have encountered some substantial drops here and there, but I'm finding myself enjoying this version even more than my prior attempts on PS4 and PS5 (and I loved those attempts).

Having spoken to some friends that are absolutely head-over-heels for this game, I know that I am very much still in the early stages of what Elden Ring has to offer, and there's every chance that I'll butt up against another roadblock down the line and bring save file four to an end.

items.title: Tencent wants to create its own Baldur's Gate 3 and Elden Ring - betting on long-term collaboration with studios
items.summary: Tencent intends to support promising studios for years to cultivate teams capable of creating games on the level of Baldur's Gate 3 and Elden Ring.
items.content:
0 Source: Steam 7 October 2026, 09:50 Dmitry Krivov Tencent intends to support promising studios for years to cultivate teams capable of creating games on the level of Baldur's Gate 3 and Elden Ring.

Tencent Games Vice President Yongyi Zhu called Larian Studios and FromSoftware the company's 'north stars.' In an interview with The Game Business, he explained that for Tencent, talent, a unique vision, and consistent development within a specific genre are more important than the developers' origin.

According to Zhu, Larian and FromSoftware did not achieve success overnight. Larian consistently developed the Divinity series before getting the opportunity to create Baldur's Gate 3. FromSoftware went from Demon's Souls through Dark Souls and Bloodborne to Elden Ring. Tencent wants to support studios using a similar model, allowing them to refine their ideas with each new game.

The company is ready to collaborate with a team if it sees the potential for it to become a leader in a specific genre. This may not happen with the first or even the second game – Tencent is counting on many years of development.

At the same time, the company will continue to use a service model with long-term game support and small teams during the riskiest production stages. The goal is not one big hit, but studios capable of releasing major games for years.

items.title: New Steam Soulslike Blends Elden Ring With Minecraft, And It’s an MMO
items.summary: A brand-new Steam soulslike blends the best of Elden Ring and Minecraft, turning it into an MMORPG in the process.
items.content:
New Steam Soulslike Blends Elden Ring With Minecraft, And It’s an MMO From GameRant (Written by Daniel Morris) on October 7, 2026 | OpenCritic

A brand-new Steam soulslike has taken some of the best elements of Elden Ring and Minecraft , put them into a blender, and come out the other side with an exciting MMORPG. Dark Craft comes from Take Top Entertainment and looks like one of the most exciting upcoming Steam games right now

Dark Craft represents a step-up in ambition for developer Take Top Entertainment. The studio has previously only developed and published mobile games, so tackling what it describes as "the first MMORPG in the Souls-like genre" is a huge task. Fans of the best soulslikes know exactly what they want from the genre, so to give them something they didn't know they wanted would be a massive achievement.

The cyberpunk genre expands with a brand-new game available now on Steam that offers an unexpected twist to the typical sci-fi formula.

Dark Craft is an upcoming free-to-play MMORPG that takes place in a dark-fantasy world with serious Elden Ring vibes. It features classic soulslike combat in an open world that is "filled with secrets and dangers: monsters are ruthless, and other players can become either allies or enemies." items.title: Hell Is Officially Breaking Loose For The Gaming Industry Thanks To AI
items.summary: Viral games like Minecraft inside Elden Ring, PS5 emulators, and recent jailbreaks do not bode well for Sony, Microsoft, or Nintendo
items.content:
By Patricia Hernandez Published Oct 6, 2026, 2:30 PM EDT Patricia is the former editor-in-chief of Kotaku , where she spent a decade writing and editing. Prior to that, she served as the Culture Editor at Polygon , and as a reporter at The Verge . Hernandez specializes in Pokémon TCG, Nintendo, and offbeat internet culture stories. News Viral games like Minecraft inside Elden Ring, PS5 emulators, and recent jailbreaks can all be tied to Claude in some way

Graphic: Grant Walkup/Polygon | Source images: Sony Interactive Entertainment PlayStation 5 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 17 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap There's an upheaval happening in the video game industry right now, and it's a major threat to publishers and video game developers alike. The outcome of this paradigm shift won't be fully evident for years, but the cause is obvious: Artificial intelligence has advanced faster than anyone anticipated.

Perhaps you've witnessed this seismic event without even realizing it. The last week or so has seen an explosion of projects that combine mainstream video games into fully playable experiences that don't even sound real. Super Mario 64 in Elden Ring . Tony Hawk's Pro Skater in Call of Duty. Minecraft inside Pokémon. Marvel's Spider-Man inside Batman: Arkham Asylum .

All of these fever-dream amalgamations are the product of Claude Opus 5.5, which was released back on Sept. 22. Opus is powerful enough that users can reverse-engineer projects at incredible speed. What Opus does is technically possible for a human, but would normally take years. Opus instead needs only a few minutes to figure out how game developers built the gameplay mechanics and infrastructure holding together relatively modern video games.

Many of these games shouldn't be compatible with one another, as they are composed of different building blocks. After Opus figures out how a game works, it can essentially build a script bridge that translates each individual game's quirks, like the animation and physics, into a language that the other game can understand. Critically, much of this has been made possible by the release of third-party tools like the Universal Modder, which streamlines all the processes an AI needs to combine games into a single package.

As these gaming mashups proliferate, Sony has found itself at the center of an intellectual property fight. The same technology that makes those game combinations possible is also partially to blame for the sudden advances in PlayStation 5 emulators on PC. Projects like SharpEmu and KytyPS5 are both human-driven efforts built from scratch, and these tools allow PCs to boot and run PS5 games at native 4K resolution.

These emulators have limitations, and some of the earliest playable game projects can be glitchy. The innovations nonetheless undergird more pinpointed efforts to make games like Infamous: Second Son and Marvel's Wolverine stable enough to play. Before Claude was pulled into the picture to generate fixes, games like Demon's Souls couldn't even reach the character creation screen on PC.

As PS5 emulators make strides, Sony is also contending with worrying progress on the PS5 jailbreak front. Breaking free from the hardware ecosystem has been possible for a while now, but pulling it off has been somewhat prohibitive for average gamers. A new exploit called Relapse allows PS5 owners to gain kernel access to the system without the use of a PC, straight from the console's own interface. Hackers do have to use systems with older firmware, but the firmware version number is recent enough that most of the PS5's major releases this year could be pirated on the platform.

Relapse was authored by humans, but the exploit is inextricably linked to AI. Jailbroken devices make it possible for vibe coders to make and distribute emulators, recompilation projects, and other home-brew apps that would normally take a long time to develop. And users can get Super Mario ported to PS5 while optimizing those game files to be nearly 50% smaller than their official counterparts.

These are all unprecedented innovations, but they come with caveats. Many of the viral projects aren't necessarily playable public experiences, nor are they fully stable builds. Still, if this is what is possible in only a few weeks after a major AI breakthrough, one can only imagine where things will be a few months from now. DMCA takedowns can only go so far when seemingly no game is safe. Factor in that the law hasn't quite caught up with AI developments, and you've got to imagine this ordeal has gaming executives sweating.

items.title: How Game of Thrones and Dark Souls echo eighty years of gothic decay
Skyrim modder forgoes trend of AI-powered crossovers, brings Elden Ring's combat to the RPG himself and earns rave reviews: "Holy peak"
items.content:
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Bethesda) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter As the wait for The Elder Scrolls 6 presses on, Skyrim players are still finding ways to spice the 14-year-old RPG up with mods – like one that brings Elden Ring combat to the game.

Yes, you read that right… FromSoftware 's notoriously brutal combat in Bethesda's, uh, far more forgiving formula. A fan reveals the mod over on X , noting that it's "fully playable," with a clip of the crossover creation in action. "This isn't a passthrough or any fancy tricks," they write. "Someone straight up remade Elden Ring's player controller in Rust and can now be added to any game!" So, put simply, this is the product of players themselves.

There's the first, "Funny-Bones" over on GitHub , who conjured up the "Elden Ring player movement and combat," as he calls it, using Rust – a programming language, which can then be applied to virtually any other game. Then, there's the modder who did just that, leading to the impressive video of the Dovahkiin fighting Tarnished-style that's circulating social media now. It's impressive, and doubly so considering the whole generative AI trend.

Skyrim x Elden Ring 🚨 Elden Ring combat is now FULLY playable in Skyrim via a mod. This isnt a passthrough or any fancy tricks. Someone straight up remade Elden Ring's player controller in Rust and can now be added to any game! https://t.co/lxRH8kGVYR October 6, 2026

You know, the one that's seeing countless people try and generate games into other games? If you're lucky enough to have not witnessed it yet yourself, it basically involves folks taking popular titles and merging them with others. For example, just have a look at this post that supposedly shows "the entire" Minecraft game running in Elden Ring. Spoiler alert: it's AI slop, and not a playable mod at all, unfortunately.

The Skyrim mod should be, though, as its poster notes he'll be uploading it "soon" – and fans are, well, fans . One person puts it perfectly in the replies: "Holy peak." Others dub the project "insane," while more comment on how "cool" it is. As for when we'll all get to check it out for ourselves, there's no telling. Fingers crossed it's soon, because who doesn't love dying to a mere bandit a million times over?

The Elder Scrolls 6's reappearance won't stop the Bethesda fan making their own Daggerfall-style RPG 4,000 hours into Elden Ring, streamer commissions a custom mod so he can beat it another 726 times Morrowind-like RPG whose devs gave up waiting for Elder Scrolls 6 launches to positive Steam rating Searching for other ways to spice your base game up? Browse through our handy roundup of the best Skyrim mods out there to download for free.

Anna Koselke Social Links Navigation Staff Writer After spending years with her head in various fantastical realms' clouds, Anna studied English Literature and then Medieval History at the University of Edinburgh, going on to specialize in narrative design and video game journalism as a writer. She has written for various publications since her postgraduate studies, including Dexerto, Fanbyte, GameSpot, IGN, PCGamesN, and more. When she's not frantically trying to form words into coherent sentences, she's probably daydreaming about becoming a fairy druid and befriending every animal or she's spending a thousand (more) hours traversing the Underdark in Baldur's Gate 3. If you spot her away from her PC, you'll always find Anna with a fantasy book, a handheld video game console of some sort, and a Tamagotchi or two on hand.

items.content:
The roar of the Red Lion echoes to the heavens.

He built his might out of love and loyalty, an unstoppable force that bade the stars to halt at the cry of a true champion. And in the Wailing Dunes, the loyalty he shared with others freed him from a fate worse than death. Now, the power of this greatest of Carian generals can rest in the palm of your hand. Standing 12 cm (4.7 in) tall, Starscourge Radahn is stylized figure that features simple articulation, interchangeable left- and right-hand parts that hold his Starscourge Greatsword, his detachable scrawny steed, and a dedicated display stand. Produced with the super-deformed proportions of the FIGURARTS Mini series, Starscourge Radahn is molded from quality PVC and ABS with exact attention to detail paid even at this miniature size. His golden armor, his raging snarl, even the gravity crests on his blades can be made out with perfect clarity. Pre-orders for this charming miniature figure are available now on the Bandai Namco Store. Do not tary, every other limited edition in this series has sold out. *This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: New Elden Ring Mini Replicas Arrive: Malenia, Messmer & Wylder
items.summary: Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the l
items.content:
Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the legendary Blade of Miquella, to the fearsome Messmer the Impaler, and the indominable warriors of Nightreign, these finely crafted collectibles capture the artistry and atmosphere that have made the Elden Ring universe unforgettable.

Elden Ring - Arm of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Celebrate the unmatched elegance and strength of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this exquisite 1/3 scale replica of her prosthetic arm from Elden Ring. Meticulously sculpted and finished, the piece highlights every refined detail - from the intricate golden engravings to the articulated armor plating that defines her graceful yet deadly form. The arm's metallic sheen and subtle weathering evoke the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior. Presented on a simple black display base, it offers an elegant way to showcase this symbol of unwavering resolve.

Elden Ring - Helmet of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Honor the legacy of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this meticulously crafted 1/3 scale replica of her legendary helmet from Elden Ring. Every detail reflects the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior, from the intricate engravings to the elegant winged crest that defines her unmistakable silhouette. The helmet's metallic finish and subtle weathering capture the essence of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's battle-worn armor. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant and timeless way to display this symbol of strength and determination.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree - Helmet of Messmer Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Embrace the dark majesty of Messmer the Impaler with this finely detailed 1/3 scale replica of his distinctive helmet from Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. Sculpted with precision, the piece captures the menacing elegance of Messmer the Impaler's design - from the elongated horns and ornate patterns to the burnished metallic finish that reflects his fiery power. The helmet's intricate craftsmanship evokes the regal yet fearsome aura of the Impaler himself. Presented on a simple black display stand, it provides a refined presentation worthy of this symbol of divine wrath.

Elden Ring Nightreign - Helmet of Wylder Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Enter the shadowed realm of Elden Ring Nightreign with this finely crafted 1/3 scale replica of the Wylder Helmet, an iconic piece of armor worn by the wandering knights of the darkened lands. This high-quality collectible captures every intricate detail of the original design, from the weathered metallic finish to the subtle engravings that mark its storied past. The helmet features a fabric neck veil, adding texture and realism to the piece. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant way to showcase its imposing form.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. Whether your allegiance lies with Malenia, your fascination belongs to Messmer, or you're drawn to the mysteries of Nightreign, these collectibles are the perfect way to bring a piece of the Lands Between to your collection.

Which replica will earn a place on your shelf?

*This products are available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: The next game from Hoyoverse sure looks like someone put Elden Ring's clothes on Monster Hunter
items.content:
Who among us doesn't love to sever the Dreadnodus?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Hoyoverse) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter As the opening reveal of this year's Gamescom Opening Night Live, HoYoverse brought its first official look at Nodusfall—a change of pace for the gacha game behemoth that looks a little bit Elden Ring , a lot bit Monster Hunter, and a whole pile of proper nouns added for good measure.

While I like to think it takes more to catch my attention than forcefully mashing together two things I think are neat, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't tempted by the idea. If there's one thing Monster Hunter monsters have been missing, it's FromSoft-style primordial depression.

Watch On From the looks of things, there's more than enough metaphysical malaise to go around in Nodusfall. The laws of divinity have apparently frayed, plunging creation into a state of cosmic disarray. There are 10 suns now. Ideally, there's only supposed to be one of those. Not great!

Luckily for those of us who like to be given an excuse to try to fight a lizard 30 times our size, all that profound devastation seems to have produced a wide selection of giant, charismatic creatures to swordfight alongside your friends. In the reveal trailer embedded above, I saw giant bears, some sort of giant pack foxes, a horned, winged manticore, and a dragon or two (giant). I don't yet know how Nodusfall's progression works, but if I'm not allowed to harvest all their individual pieces and turn them into pants, I'm going to feel personally betrayed.

While the glimpses of combat shown in the footage looks like it hews pretty closely to the pace and rhythm of Monster Hunter, Nodusfall does seem to be dropping a few original elements into the mix. At one point, one of the player characters uses some sort of transformation ability to become a giant, armored knight in the middle of a hunt. And later, two players perform an elaborate, paired execution animation.

Nodusfall isn't Elden Ring, Monster Hunter or a typical HoYoverse game—it's something very different HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' All the key details on HoYo's co-op monster slayer Nodusfall What remains to be seen is what sort of monetization scheme Nodusfall will be wrapped in—something that HoYoverse's history doesn't exactly inspire confidence about. If I have to do gacha pulls for a gunlance, I'm going to have a hard time.

Nodusfall doesn't have much of an online presence yet, so it'll likely be a while before we can expect a release date.

items.title: Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching 28th August on Nintendo Switch 2
items.content:
The Lands Between—a place of myth, gods, and broken dreams. Long ago, Queen Marika and her divine offspring reigned here, but since the Elden Ring was shattered, the world has fallen into decay. Now, the land whispers for a King.

The ‘Tarnished’, long exiled, are finally seeing the light of Grace once more. Step into this hauntingly beautiful realm, unravel its ancient mysteries, and rise as the one true Elden Lord.

The ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition game arrives on the Nintendo Switch™ 2 system on 28th August .

The Lands Between are part of a vast continent, where magnificent open fields and huge dungeons with complex three-dimensional designs are seamlessly connected. As you explore, the joy of discovering unknown and overwhelming threats awaits you.

Mastery of the terrain and knowledge of its secrets can help you overcome enemies and defeat formidable bosses—or lead invading players into traps.

An epic drama born from a myth created by George R.R. Martin The founding mythology of Elden Ring was written by George R. R. Martin and adapted into a rich multilayered story. Intersecting goals and desires between the characters create an intense narrative that weaves throughout the Lands Between. The events of the game can unravel in many ways—depending on your interventions.

Combat is simple to learn yet offers hidden depths of dexterity. As you seek to become the Elden Lord, you’ll need to explore the balance between attacking, avoiding damage, using a wide variety of weapons, spells, summons, and perfecting your timing to take advantage of your opponents’ weaknesses.

Create and build your own character In addition to customising the appearance of your character, there are countless ways to combine the weapons, armour, usable items, and magic that you equip. You can develop your character according to your play style.

No matter if you prefer bold physical confrontation, tactical spellcasting, or the subtle art of stealth, you’ll be able to find gear that supports your choices.

Traverse together with other Nintendo Switch 2 players. You can play with up to two other Tarnished as your cooperative teammates, either by inviting them using a shared password or by summoning them from a pool of nearby community members.

There are also ample opportunities to face off against other players, either through co-op invasions, invited duels, or the many player battle options available in the three Colosseums.

If you’d like to learn more or begin your journey to the Lands Between by pre-ordering the Tarnished Edition, please check out the link below.

items.title: Is Elden Ring the best of the Souls series?
items.summary: Is Elden Ring the best Soulslike game ever made? Explore how FromSoftware reinvented the genre with open-world freedom, epic boss fights, and unmatched player choice.
items.content:
For over a decade FromSoftware have created an iconic system of gameplay that influenced countless other games.

For over a decade FromSoftware have created an iconic system of gameplay that influenced countless other games and inspired players of all ages.

Let’s take a look at how ELDEN RING has elevated and perfected the original Souls series formula and explore if ELDEN RING could be the best of the entire Souls series.

The majority of the games were designed by Hidetaka Miyazaki to give players the experience of exploring dark and majestic fantasy worlds full of danger.

There’s also a strong focus on difficulty, world structure, boss fights, and player builds.

The difficulty of the Souls series stems from their combat design. They emphasize deliberate attack and evasion in response to enemy movement, which tends to be quick, fierce, and punishing for players who find themselves out of position at the wrong moment. Players need to carefully observe and learn their foes’ patterns, then react to exploit certain specific attack openings without leaving themselves open as well.

This type of careful, evasive gameplay mimics the danger and strategy of real hand-to-hand combat and the high stakes keeps the tension and excitement rising in each fight. It’s not as simple as playing out a power fantasy where enemies easily fall to repeated mindless button mashing. For most players, this difficulty means that the feeling of mastering Souls series combat is a rush of pure accomplishment.

In the earlier Souls series games , levels are massive, interconnected linear paths. These paths often have several branching paths that reward exploration and puzzle solving, but are limited in terms of true open field exploration, as it’s necessary to follow a specific set order of levels, usually connected by a hub area where players can regroup, level up and open new paths, to progress throughout the game.

In the best Souls series games , carefully studying the environment and enemy behavior can lead to hidden areas or items, a particular strength of the Dark Souls series, and many players consider level design that rewards careful exploration to be a critical feature of Dark Souls-like games .

Throughout the Souls series , boss battles are powerful climatic moments that put a player’s abilities to the test. In the Dark Souls series , specifically, from the Asylum Demon to Slave Knight Gael , the Dark Souls bosses are encounters that inspire fear, awe, pity, and wonder.

Bosses also act as progression gates that require a certain level of fluency with the game’s combat system before the player can continue to explore. Once a player reaches a boss gate, they must either muster the skill to defeat that boss, or continue to practice and grind on earlier enemies.

Unlike the average enemy that players must face in a limited area not much wider than a typical hallway, bosses are frequently found in massive arenas. Bosses in the Souls series also tend to have enhanced abilities that require the player to adapt to attacks that cover huge areas or have extended reach. This ferocity and enlarged battlefield gives the designers space to create exciting, multi-phase duels that are unforgettably intense.

These boss fights also act as a check on the player’s build. No matter which weapons or elements a player prefers, massive and powerful bosses require adaptation.

Experienced players understand how each type of stat affects their damage output and they use all of the gear at their disposal to create a move set that fits their style and is powerful enough to take down bosses.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE

items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stormveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.
